findings: The candidate source encoder consumes triangle records containing three vertex pointers, with edge boundary flags. Its earlier iterator branch does not establish point-cloud support.
Grid setup uses an eight-child spatial tree; its rounding import and complete admission behavior remain unresolved.
Triangle admission visits overlapping cells and keeps the nearer absolute signed-distance result per source at a corner.

Corner reduction prefers non-boundary source contributions when present, otherwise uses boundary contributions; signed distances are averaged and the combined direction is normalized. Initialization and normalization edge cases require further trace.
Leaf extraction uses strict negative-distance sign masks and standard Marching Cubes connectivity.

Edge position arithmetic uses endpoint surface projections: choose the nearer endpoint when its absolute distance is strictly below one quarter of the largest cell dimension, otherwise average projections, with final Float32 coordinates.
